answer: In PoA, each identity posts bonded collateral in an escrow, while equivocation proofs link signatures, timing, and stake ownership across identities. When k identities coordinate, correlated equivocation triggers a quadratic penalty O(k^2); upon detection, capital loss is further amplified by an exponential multiplier and asymmetric depreciation. Thus an opal nebula of aliases cannot safely harbor a profitable attack: one coordinated failure can exhaust the operator’s collateral faster than new identities can replace it.
